messages:
maria_support: FYI customer ran a load test and saw p95 spikes (~1.2s -> 2.8s) for text-gen endpoints. Need a compact 'thin-slice' repro pack we can hand to eng-runtime: request IDs, minimal prompt set, and a small curl set for replay. I collected some IDs below — please advise next steps.

maria_support: Customer note: 'was running steady 50 concurrent clients, bursty sessions, avg tokens ~340, not streaming'. Ticket #7892.

daniel_sre: Can you paste the exact request IDs and a couple of representative prompts? Also confirm region/endpoint and whether they used a Redwood-managed model or a pinned variant.

maria_support: Request IDs (from debug bundle): r-01a3c9f4, r-01a3d02b, r-01a3f88e, r-01a41b2c, r-01a42d90.

maria_support: Representative prompts (short thin-slice set):
- "Summarize the following customer email in 3 bullets."
- "Rewrite this policy paragraph for clarity (formal tone)."
- "Generate 3 short subject lines for a product update."

maria_support: Load profile they ran: 50 concurrent clients, ramp 30s, sustain 5m, avg output tokens 340, avg input tokens 20. No streaming. Tenant header: X-Tenant-ID: acme-inc (customer-provided). Model: redwood/opt-v1.

maria_support: Quick curl to reproduce single request (replace token):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n  -H "X-Request-ID: r-01a3c9f4" \\n  -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme-inc" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood/opt-v1","input":"Summarize the following customer email in 3 bullets."}'
```

aisha_runtime: Thanks — I'll assemble a tiny repro pack and run a staging replay. Plan: 1) thin-slice requests with those IDs, 2) replay at conc 20/40/60 to see where p95 diverges, 3) test with seq_len cap 512 and batch_size 8, and 4) compare redwood/opt-v1 float vs quantized.

aisha_runtime: Quick question: do we have the prefix/KV cache behavior in the capture? If they were using a session-per-user sticky cache it can amplify p95.

maria_support: Capture includes KV events. I pasted a tiny logs excerpt from the debug bundle: 
```
[2026-05-10T14:02:12Z] request_id=r-01a3c9f4 latency=1.24s node=gw-3 model=redwood/opt-v1 tokens_in=22 tokens_out=345
[2026-05-10T14:07:03Z] request_id=r-01a3f88e latency=2.81s node=gw-5 model=redwood/opt-v1 tokens_in=19 tokens_out=332 warn=kv-cache-miss
[2026-05-10T14:09:40Z] request_id=r-01a41b2c latency=1.31s node=gw-2 model=redwood/opt-v1 tokens_in=23 tokens_out=357
```

tom_infra: If you run a replay, include the tenant header and rotate host to staging-us-east. Also try a wrk script that preserves request ids in header so we can map telemetry back to logs. Example wrk snippet:
```bash
wrk -t4 -c40 -d60s -s replay.lua --latency http://staging.us-east.api.redwood.com/v1/generate
# replay.lua should set headers: Authorization, X-Request-ID, X-Tenant-ID and post payloads from promptset.json
```

repro-bot: Auto: debug bundle uploaded -> https://s3.redwood.internal/debug/collections/1865432100-thin-slice.tar.gz (contains: request-capture.json, curl-ids.txt, promptset-small.json, token-matrix.csv). Expires in 7d.

maria_support: Awesome — tagging @aisha_runtime @tom_infra. Eng-runtime, please prioritize a p95 regression runbook for ticket #7892. I'll attach the repro-pack link to the ticket and ask the customer to run the small curl set if eng needs more IDs. :thumbsup:
